description: An oil-style painting, edge to edge. In the centre a mounted man in a tricorn hat with a white plume, long wavy hair and blue-and-gold plate armour rears a white horse. Both sides are packed with rows of soldiers in grey-blue coats, tricorn hats and long muskets with bayonets. Behind them a dark sky of smoke and fire, with a walled town with towers burning on the left. Only text is a small sparkle logo in the bottom-right corner. Nothing gory.
reason: Shows an early-modern battle: tricorn hats, flintlock muskets with bayonets in rank, and a rider in blue-and-gold plate with a periwig-length hairstyle. That is roughly the 1690s to 1720s, not the 1098 Crusader siege of Antioch. Redraw with First Crusade-era dress and arms (mail, kite shields, lances, medieval walls) and no firearms or tricorns.
